title: The session event stream
summary: The plugin keeps a ring of the session's events (writes with their undo, refusals, the kill switch, handovers, behaviours, notes, answers); session.log merges it with the tools' log, session.note adds a marker and session.wait blocks until the player answers or something happens.

demand.note: The bridge's own event ring and npc.* events are part of the world event feed.

rows.note: session_wait from one process while another called game_status.

limits: A ring of 1000 events, with dropped for a reader that fell behind.

title: Source recorder
summary: test.record.start, read and stop sample fresh V, selected actors and the camera on 100 ms deadlines, plus the taps' channels, into a private ring and chunk files, so the coordinator can read what happened between turns.

rows.note: invalid 0, no gaps, count_detail reconciles; 25 missed deadlines and 2 drops under memory pressure.

limits: One 512-slot ring of 8192-byte payloads; 1 MiB JSONL chunks under the runtime folder's recordings.
Explicit autonomous candidate only; missed deadlines are counted, never filled from a cache.

unknowns.question: What do sampling cost, achieved cadence and teardown look like in game?

title: Subtitle and voice taps
summary: The recorder's subtitles and voice channels observe source notifications, the controller's delivery and the line widget's creation, text and removal, plus script voice requests and reaction callers.

rows.note: A nearby NPC fight was seen through voice.requested.
The full subtitle chain, attributed to the stand-in.
The ellipsis came through garbled in Borg 3; the CLI prints ASCII JSON since 0.8.18.

limits: No audible-silence claim; Wwise hooks are a separate follow-up.

title: Face submission tap
summary: The face channel records script face submissions, resets and the bridge's resends for actors and passers-by.
limits: Submissions only: no evaluated-face reader is claimed (R3's applied-input probe is a follow-up).

title: UI channel
summary: The ui channel records the panel and CET consumers' state and per-area outfit identities, on change plus a 2 s heartbeat.

rows.note: The CET surfaces logged change then heartbeats, but 237 ui records were counted while 22 were listed.

quirks: Owning-window rects do not claim output-pixel transforms or occlusion.

title: Catch-up
summary: game.catchup reads everything since a cursor in one call (recorder channels, session events, the digest), with a summary line, the newest V sample, a backlog when behind, alerts and counts that reconcile with the lists.

demand.note: The live feed reads catch-up with detail: true and its cursor, at most once a second, backing off when there is no more.

rows.note: Worked, but with the ui channel on each page fell behind real time and 'V latest' was minutes stale.
Behind real time by 392 records with backlog; live V position; caught up in three calls.

known_issues.summary: Review of 0.8.22 (Medium): a cursor with history but no supervisor totals (0.8.21's shape) read as complete zeros. Fixed in 2ff42305: it carries supervisor_totals_partial, run_totals_complete and history_complete are false, and the message says the totals are incomplete. Unverified in game.

improvements.summary: The full output is too long to read every turn; a compact summary client (Borg 2 used its own script).

title: Game-events probe
summary: test.events records the hooks the game-events research recommends (deaths, combat, heat, district, vehicles, journal, dialogue, calls, time) log-only, in a ring of their own; test.save.identity and test.companion.probe are the other session-15 probes.

known_issues.summary: The probes are compiled into every package's DLL (refused there without allow_test_hooks); remove them or move them into XF Lab once XF Core lands.
The delayed listener on dialogue choice hubs never delivered a record for the game's own hubs; 0.8.10 polls instead, cause unknown.

notes: Session 15 answered most of the event and save-identity rows (game events' questions-only-the-game-can-answer).

title: World event feed
summary: A subscribable feed of what happens in the world: V's district and interior changes, combat, kills and knockdowns, crimes and heat, vehicle use and purchases, calls and dialogue choices, fact changes, time, weather and loads.

demand.note: A world event feed; the graded hooks and a minimal set of twelve event kinds are designed. Gaps: interior entry is polled, no 'any fact changed' hook, dialogue picks inferred.

title: Read-only recorder status
summary: A read-only command answered on the bridge thread (no game-thread call, no lease, no ack) that reports whether the recorder is active and its current run: { active, run, session, world, channels, start, latest, stopReason }, so an observer can find the run to read with game.catchup.
priority_reason: The maintainer: Holotable must work in realtime; its live view only waits on this. Small, bridge-thread only.

demand.note: Holotable's Live game row polls it every 5 s, only while the view is shown. Today InfoJson() and Status() expose no recorder state, and game.catchup needs a positive run.

title: Published probe and scene results (observe.result)
summary: A bounded observe.result session event with the command, the caller's cid and the result whenever a writer calls world_probe, scene_read or world_district, adding no game-thread work.

demand.note: Lets Holotable draw what sessions already asked, at no extra game cost.

title: Wall-clock time in the run manifest
summary: The recorder run manifest carries a wall-clock mapping for its QPC clock (for example start_at, the ISO time at start_s), so replay tools can place wall-clock-timed items on the recording timeline.

demand.note: Agents and the Story Engine may publish items in wall-clock time; live uses recorder.status start.at, replay has no mapping today.

title: Game time on recorder samples
summary: The recorder's V samples (or a 1 Hz heartbeat) carry the game's own clock (game_time_s), so tools can align game-clock items, such as the Story Engine's shadow-mode simulation, with recorded and live observations.

demand.note: Read alongside the existing sample on the game thread (no extra call). Until then producers stamp with the recording clock.

title: Actor identity on recorder samples
summary: The actors channel carries each actor's character record id, affiliation and crowd flag, once per actor (or on first sample), so observers can tell who an actor is.

demand.note: Story Engine shadow mode binds simulated residents to recorded actors; Holotable shows affiliation in the People layer.
Shadow mode reads these from the recorder (live and replay) through Holotable's model.

title: Deaths and knockdowns on the recorder
summary: A recorder channel (or incident kind) for deaths and knockdowns with victim, instigator and cause, with positions.

demand.note: Story Engine shadow mode reacts to deaths; Holotable draws them as events.
Shadow mode reads these from the recorder (live and replay) through Holotable's model.

unknowns.question: Which game event or listener reports this without new game-thread polling (an event the engine already raises, read where the recorder already samples)?

title: Combat start and end on the recorder
summary: Combat start and end events with participants.

demand.note: Shadow mode reads these from the recorder (live and replay) through Holotable's model.

unknowns.question: Which game event or listener reports this without new game-thread polling (an event the engine already raises, read where the recorder already samples)?

title: Crimes and police heat on the recorder
summary: Crime events with offender and the police heat level over time.

demand.note: Shadow mode reads these from the recorder (live and replay) through Holotable's model.
